evil_mirror_analysis.note: The good/evil mirror in LM2 Torah 3 is structurally precise. Package 1 (פדיון/המתקה) directly sweetens and dissolves Package 3 (מדת הדין/מחין דקטנות). The instrument of the mirror is the vowel system: cholam (three Havayot = Package 1) sweetens the three Elokim at the throat (Package 3). analysis_notes.torah_structure_note: LM2 Torah 3 is a concise, tightly argued teaching (10 lines). Its structure is predominantly eitza (causal/sequential): middat hadin constrains healing → pidyon sweetens the din → healing becomes possible. However, within this causal chain there are three critical bechina moments where the Rebbe identifies parallel natures: (1) חולם = המתקה [the vowel IS sweetening], (2) שלש הויות and חולם share the same gematria = same nature, (3) שלשה אלקים שבגרון = מחין דקטנות [the Elokim-names ARE constricted consciousness]. These bechina nodes form the three packages above. The broader Torah argument follows the classic eitza structure: Package 3 (evil/constraint) → eitza → Package 1 (sweetening/pidyon) → eitza → Package 2 (healing/permission).
analysis_notes.gematria_note: The Torah uses gematria as a bechina proof tool: 'וְרַפֹּא יְרַפֵּא (עִם שְׁתֵּי הַתֵּבוֹת) מִסְפַּר פִּדְיוֹן נֶפֶשׁ' — the gematria of the double expression 'verafo yeraphei' equals the gematria of 'pidyon nefesh'. This numerical equivalence IS a bechina proof: these two are expressions of the same spiritual reality. Similarly, 'חוֹלָם גִּימַטְרִיָּא שָׁלֹשׁ הֲוָיוֹת' — the cholam equals three Havayot in gematria, establishing their shared essential nature.
